CONTEXT — a real customer migration completed today and reported SUCCESS while the customer's main site showed a browser certificate warning and then an Apache default page. Root causes are known and confirmed on the live box. Your job is to make each of these failures IMPOSSIBLE TO REPORT AS SUCCESS, and where cheap, to auto-remediate.

Read the file first and follow its existing idioms exactly: the `sh(conn, cmd, timeoutMs)` helper (returns `{code,stdout,stderr}`, never throws), `shOk`, `say()` for customer-facing progress lines, `report(pct, step, logLine)`, the `pending[]` array of `{domain, why, fix}`, and the existing end-of-run summary. Match the established comment style: explain WHY, cite the real incident.

Implement, in priority order:

**1. HONEST SUCCESS SCORING (highest value).**
Today the run logged `Sites actually serving: 4/4` while SIX domains were dark; it also logged `Sites we could not publish automatically — content.revsports.ca, dealerleads.me, new.nexis.revsports.ca, reel.revsports.ca, stg.studionexis.com, studionexis.com`. The denominator was "domains we chose to publish", so the metric can never fail.
- Denominator MUST be every domain the SOURCE served (the discovered/inventoried set), not the generated-config set.
- Report `served/total` against that, and list the unserved ones by name.
- Find how the migration's terminal status is set and introduce a distinct outcome when any source domain is unserved or any check below fails — e.g. `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` — instead of a clean success. If the Migration.status column is a constrained enum in prisma/schema.prisma you MUST NOT edit the schema; in that case keep status DONE but set a clear, structured summary field/flag the UI can key off, and say so in your report.

**2. DEFAULT-PAGE DETECTION.**
The existing "make a real request to each domain" check passed for a domain that was serving the Apache2 Debian Default Page. Treat as NOT serving: Apache "It works!"/"Apache2 Debian Default Page"/"Apache2 Ubuntu Default Page", nginx "Welcome to nginx!", and empty/near-empty bodies. Also flag TLS name mismatch: if the cert served for a domain does not cover that domain (CN/SAN), that domain is NOT serving — today studionexis.com was served nexis.revsports.ca's cert.

**3. SYSTEMD UNIT PRE-FLIGHT — the `203/EXEC` class.**
Today `nexis-next.service` had `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node /opt/nexis/node_modules/next/dist/bin/next start -p 3105` and `/usr/local/bin/node` did not exist on the target (only `/usr/bin/node` v20). It crash-looped 78 times and the migration still reported success.
BEFORE enabling/starting migrated units: for every unit we are about to enable, parse `ExecStart=`, `ExecStartPre=`, `ExecStartPost=` and extract the leading ABSOLUTE executable path. If it does not exist on the target:
  - if a binary of the same basename exists elsewhere on the target (check `command -v <basename>`), create a symlink at the expected path and log it plainly;
  - else if the path exists on the SOURCE, copy it across (there is existing rsync/transfer machinery — reuse it);
  - else record a blocking `pending[]` entry naming the unit and the missing path.
Be defensive parsing unit files: handle `ExecStart=-/path`, `@`, `+`, `!` prefixes, quoted paths, and multi-line continuations. Ignore non-absolute (PATH-resolved) commands.

**4. UNIT HEALTH GATE — the "never built" class.**
`/opt/nexis` had no `.next` production build, so even with node fixed the unit exits 1 in a loop. After enabling/starting migrated units, wait briefly then assert for each: state is `active` (not `activating`/`failed`) AND its systemd restart counter is not climbing. For any unit that is crash-looping, capture the last few journal lines and surface them as a `pending[]` entry with the actual error text — a service that has restarted 78 times must never be silent. Where the error is the recognisable Next.js "Could not find a production build in the '.next' directory", say so explicitly and give `next build` as the fix.

**5. CONFLICTING WEB SERVERS.**
Today the run re-enabled `apache2` from the source while we generated an nginx config; apache2 then failed to bind and sat `enabled + failed`, a latent hazard on reboot. When we generate our own nginx configuration, explicitly disable/mask the other web servers we did not choose (`apache2`, `httpd`, `caddy`, `lighttpd`) rather than re-enabling them, and log that we did.

**6. HEARTBEATS.**
The run sat silent at 89% for ten minutes during a package install. For the long steps (package install, image transfer, certificate issuance), emit periodic progress so the customer never sees a frozen bar. Keep it cheap — a line every ~30-60s naming what is still running is enough.

Finally append a dated section to `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` recording these five incidents AND — importantly — noting that the `/usr/local/bin/node` failure was already documented after a previous incident and recurred anyway, which is why it is now an executable pre-flight check rather than a doc entry.

- Do NOT git commit or push.
- Do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma, lib/**, app/**, components/**, or any worker file other than worker/migrate-real.ts. Another process is editing those right now.
- Preserve every existing behaviour and log line unless the brief says to change it. This code runs against real customer servers — favour "report loudly" over "silently attempt something clever". Never take a destructive action on the customer's data.
- NOTE: near the top of `ensurePackages` I just added `APT_ENV`/`APT_OPTS` constants (NEEDRESTART_MODE etc.) — leave those intact and reuse them for any apt you invoke.

Report back concisely: what you implemented, the new outcome/flag semantics for a partially-successful migration, and anything you could not do because it needed a file outside your scope.

2	
3	Real-world failures observed running the lift-and-shift migration against a live
4	customer server, with the fix for each. **This is the acceptance criteria for the
5	migration engine**: a customer should be able to migrate, point DNS, and have their
6	site serve over HTTPS with no server access.
7	
8	Source of truth for these findings: a real migration on 2026-07-25 from a
9	HestiaCP/Hostinger box (Debian, nginx 1.25, 72.62.69.9) to a fresh Nxeon VPS

14	## The architectural lesson
15	
16	**Do not blind-copy the source's `/etc/nginx` (or `/etc/apache2`) tree.** That single
17	behaviour caused roughly half of the failures below. Copying wholesale imports the
18	source's `nginx.conf`, its include layout, its panel-specific vhosts, its IP

said `Sites actually serving: 4/4`.

| 23 | **A 200 from the distribution's default page counted as "serving"** | The existing "make a real request to each domain" probe passed for a domain answering 200 with the Apache2 Debian Default Page | The probe now fetches the **body** as well as the status. Apache "It works!" / "Apache2 Debian Default Page" / "Apache2 Ubuntu Default Page" / "Apache HTTP Server Test Page", nginx "Welcome to nginx!", and empty/near-empty 2xx bodies are all **not serving**. Content is only judged on a 2xx (a 301→HTTPS or a 404 legitimately has a tiny body); short JSON/XML bodies are exempt so an API vhost is never called dark |
| 24 | **TLS name mismatch was invisible** | `studionexis.com` was served `nexis.revsports.ca`'s certificate. | 25 | **`203/EXEC` — unit enabled with a binary that does not exist here** | `nexis-next.service` had `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node …`; the target has only `/usr/bin/node` (v20, apt). | 26 | **"Never built" apps crash-loop silently** | `/opt/nexis` had no `.next` production build, so even with Node fixed the unit exits 1 forever | **Health gate after enabling.** Units settle, then `NRestarts` is sampled twice: `active` + a counter that is not climbing, or it is a blocker with the last journal lines attached. | 27 | **Two web servers, one port 80** | `apache2` was re-enabled from the source's service list while we generated an nginx config. earlier migration where the same `/usr/local/bin/node` mismatch crash-looped a unit

Done. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, and only `worker/migrate-real.ts` and `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` were touched. ## What I implemented **1. Honest success scoring.** A new `sourceDomains` set is captured right after the live source inventory (step 4b-ii), from the source's *own* merged vhost config (`inv.domains` ∪ `parseNginxDump`/`parseApacheDump` names) — before any decision about what we can publish. The final score is `served/total` against that set, the unserved names are listed by name in the log and the summary, and domains beyond the 24-name probe cap are reported as "not checked", never as serving. When the live inventory fails there is no honest denominator, so it falls back to the published set *and says so as an issue reason*. **2. Default-page + TLS-mismatch detection.** `httpProbe` now returns body as well as status (one curl, `mktemp` output file — a fixed `/tmp` name is a symlink-overwrite risk on a migrated multi-user box). `defaultPageReason` treats Apache Debian/Ubuntu default pages, the RHEL test page, `

It works!

`, `Welcome to nginx!` and empty/near-empty 2xx bodies as **not serving**; content is only judged on 2xx, and short JSON/XML is exempt so API vhosts aren't false-flagged. `servedCertNames` reads the certificate the server actually presents via `openssl s_client -servername` and `certCoversName` matches CN/SAN (`*.x` = exactly one label) — no coverage means not serving. Skipped when a container owns 443. **3. `203/EXEC` pre-flight.** `parseUnitExecPaths` handles `-`/`@`/`+`/`!` prefixes, quoted paths, backslash continuations, `ExecStart=` list resets, and ignores PATH-resolved and `%`-specifier commands. Missing binary → symlink to the `command -v` basename match → else rsync the file from the source → else a blocking entry and **the unit is not enabled at all** (enabling a known-broken unit just creates a reboot-persistent crash loop). **4. Unit health gate.** After enabling, units settle 12s, `NRestarts` is sampled twice 15s apart; `active` + non-climbing counter is the only pass. Failures carry the actual journal tail; the Next.js "Could not find a production build in the '.next' directory" case is recognised by name with `next build` as the fix. Per-unit results are now *held* until the gate rules, so a crash-looping unit can no longer land in `verifiedRunning`. **5. Conflicting web servers.** `standDownOtherWebServers` stops, disables **and masks** every other host web server (`apache2`/`httpd`/`caddy`/`lighttpd`, or `nginx` if we chose Apache), logging the `systemctl unmask` reversal. Step 11 separately refuses to re-enable a source web server that isn't the one we chose. **6. Heartbeats.** `withHeartbeat` emits one line every ~45s naming what is still running and for how long; wired into `ensurePackages` (optional `say` param, so existing call sites are unchanged), both `ensureImage` paths, and all three certbot issuance paths. ## Outcome semantics for a partial success `runRealMigration` returns `outcome: "COMPLETED" | "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` plus `outcomeReasons`, `sourceDomains`, `unservedDomains`, `blockers`, and `siteProbes[].reason`. `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` when any source domain is unserved, any was unchecked, or any migrated unit isn't running. ## What needed a file outside my scope `Migration.status` is a plain `String` in `prisma/schema.prisma` (not a Prisma enum), so the schema was never the blocker — **the writer is**. `worker/migrate.ts` hardcodes `status: "DONE"` after `runRealMigration` returns and persists *only* `summary.results` into `Migration.items.results`; both are outside my scope. So: - The structured flag that actually reaches the UI today is the **first entry of `results`**: step `Migration outcome: COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`, status `failed`, detail listing every reason. That is persisted and renderable now. - `summary.outcome` / `outcomeReasons` / `unservedDomains` / `blockers` are returned and typed but **currently dropped on the floor**. Wiring them through is a one-line change in `worker/migrate.ts` (e.g. `status: summary.outcome === "COMPLETED" ? "DONE" : "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"`, or persisting the fields into `items`) — I did not make it. The completion notification body in that file also still says "completed" unconditionally. Field notes appended as items 22–28 with a dated section, including the explicit note that the `/usr/local/bin/node` failure was already documented as item 13 (880 crash-loops, fix spelled out), recurred anyway four months later, and is now an executable pre-flight *because* a documented fix nothing reads is not a fix.
